html:
Krishnadevaraya was the emperor of Vijayanagara in south India from 1509 to 1529, the time when the empire was at its strongest and richest.

He spent much of his reign at war, and won:

  • He defeated the Deccan sultans, most famously taking the fort of Raichur from Bijapur in 1520.
  • He took forts and land from the Gajapati kings of Odisha and married a Gajapati princess.
  • He kept good terms with the Portuguese at Goa, who sold him war horses.

His capital at Hampi amazed visitors. The Portuguese traveller Domingo Paes described its markets, palaces and festivals and compared it to Rome.

He was a poet as well. He wrote the Amuktamalyada in Telugu, about a woman saint who married the god Vishnu. Eight leading poets, the Ashtadiggajas, worked at his court, and he gave to temples across the south, including Tirupati.

Some 36 years after his death, the sultans joined forces and beat Vijayanagara at the Battle of Talikota in 1565, and Hampi was sacked.
